Case_18012/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2: CT scan of the neck. A soft tissue density is seen in the subcutaneous tissue on the right side of the neck with skin thickening and adjacent fat stranding without evidence of a fluid collection.

description.short_caption: Axial CT of the neck showing subcutaneous soft tissue density with fat stranding on the right.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the neck demonstrates a soft tissue density in the subcutaneous tissue on the right side, marked by a red circle. There is associated fat stranding and skin thickening, but no clear evidence of a fluid collection or abscess. The surrounding structures, including the vertebrae and airway, appear intact.
visible_findings: soft tissue density in subcutaneous tissue

Case_18012/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1: Neck lesion at presentation (A) and after removal of the eschar (B)

description.short_caption: Neck lesion before (A) and after eschar removal (B).
description.detailed_description: This image shows two clinical photographs of a lesion on the neck. Panel A depicts an erythematous, indurated lesion with a central dark eschar surrounded by scaling and inflammation. Panel B shows the same lesion after removal of the eschar, revealing an ulcerated base with surrounding erythema and scaling. The lesion is located on the posterior neck near the hairline.
visible_findings: ulcerated base after eschar removal in panel B

Case_18012/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Figure 3b: Several intracytoplasmic bodies (arrow) are seen measuring around 2 micrometer (400x magnification). These are consistent with amastigotes. Each amastigote has a prominent kinetoplast.

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing intracytoplasmic amastigotes with prominent kinetoplasts.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image, stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), shows several intracytoplasmic bodies (amastigotes) within host cells. The amastigotes are small, measuring approximately 2 micrometers, and each contains a prominent kinetoplast, which is a distinguishing feature. The surrounding tissue includes inflammatory cells and appears to be part of a granulomatous response. The image is magnified at 400x.

Case_18012/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 3A: Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate is seen with pan-dermal granulomas (40x magnification).

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with granulomas in the dermis (40x magnification).
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with granulomas spanning the dermis. The granulomas are well-formed and distributed throughout the dermal layer. The staining highlights cellular details, with lymphocytes and plasma cells visible. The magnification is approximately 40x, providing a clear view of the inflammatory and granulomatous architecture.

Case_18012/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Figure 4: Serial photography of the neck lesion

description.short_caption: Serial photographs of a neck lesion showing progression and healing over time.
description.detailed_description: This composite image shows serial photographs of a lesion on the neck at different stages of progression and treatment. Panel A depicts the lesion at presentation, with a central eschar surrounded by erythema. Panel B shows the lesion after removal of the eschar, revealing an ulcerated base. Panels C, D, and E demonstrate progressive healing at 10 days, 2 months, and 4 months post-treatment, respectively, with decreasing erythema and resolution of the ulceration.
visible_findings: progressive reduction in erythema and lesion size in panels C, D, and E
